claim.quote: An improved value for the lifetime of the (anti-)hypertriton has been obtained using the data sample of Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 5.02 TeV collected by the ALICE experiment at the LHC.

date.locator: arXiv:1907.06906, submitted 16 July 2019; Phys. Lett. B 797 (2019) 134905

key_value.display: 0.242 ns (+0.034/-0.038 stat, +/-0.017 syst) [= 242 ps in the source's own units]
key_value.note: Converted from ps (242 ps = 0.242 ns) since 'ps' is not in the atlas's recognised time units; display preserves the source's own ps figure.
key_value.quote: The measured value, tau = 242+34-38 (stat.) +/- 17 (syst.) ps, is compatible with all the available theoretical predictions

name: (Anti-)hypertriton lifetime measurement in Pb-Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV
notes: This is an ALICE-specific hypertriton lifetime measurement; a separate, unrelated STAR-experiment hypertriton mass-difference/CPT paper (also on arXiv, coincidentally an adjacent id) was found during research and explicitly excluded from this record after its full text showed it used STAR detector data, not ALICE.

summary.plain: ALICE measured how long a rare, fragile nucleus called the hypertriton survives before decaying, using lead-lead collisions at the LHC, helping settle a long-running disagreement between earlier experiments' measurements.
summary.technical: ALICE measurement of the (anti-)hypertriton lifetime via its two-body mesonic decay channel in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 5.02 TeV: tau = 242(+34/-38 stat) +/- 17(syst) ps, compatible with available theoretical predictions and contributing to resolving the hypertriton lifetime puzzle.

title: 3_Lambda H and 3_Lambdabar Hbar lifetime measurement in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 5.02 TeV via two-body decay
why_it_matters: The hypertriton (a proton, neutron and Lambda hyperon bound together) is the lightest known hypernucleus; its lifetime, if much shorter than a free Lambda's, would point to unexpectedly strong hyperon-nucleon interactions relevant to the physics of neutron-star interiors. This measurement addresses a long-standing discrepancy between earlier, scattered lifetime measurements (the 'hypertriton lifetime puzzle').
